sources: John 20:19-22 (the evening of the first day of the week, the doors shut where the disciples were gathered, for fear; Jesus came and stood in the midst and said, “Peace be to you”; he showed them his hands and his side; the disciples were glad when they saw the Lord; “Peace be to you. As the Father hath sent me, I also send you”; he breathed on them and said, “Receive ye the Holy Ghost”). Douay-Rheims (Challoner).
Mark 14:50 and Matthew 26:56 (at his arrest, the disciples all left him and fled).
Matthew 5:23-24 (if you bring your gift to the altar and remember your brother has something against you, leave your gift, go first to be reconciled, then come and offer it).
Eirene (Greek) and shalom (Hebrew): peace, wholeness. Justin Martyr, First Apology 65 (the kiss in worship); Romans 16:16.
General Instruction of the Roman Missal 82 (the Rite of Peace before communion; the form of the gesture set by local custom).

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? when someone has let you down, what do you usually say first when you see them again?
options: that’s so human. watch what he says first.
me too, sometimes. this story goes another way.
I try to clear the air
then you’ll love this one. listen.

steps.line: On the night of the first Easter, the friends of Jesus hid in a locked room. They had run away when he was arrested. Now they were afraid.

steps.q: Suddenly the risen Jesus is standing in the room, with the friends who ran away. What does he say about their running?
o: He asks why they left him
He tells them he forgives them
steps.why: Nothing. In John’s telling his first words are an everyday greeting, and the night they ran never comes up.

steps.line: Then Jesus was standing among them, though the doors were locked. His first words were, “Peace be with you.”

steps.q: “Peace be with you” was an everyday Jewish greeting: shalom aleichem. What does shalom mean at its root?
steps.why: Shalom comes from a root meaning complete. Greeting the friends who broke faith with ‘wholeness’ mends the friendship before a word about it.

steps.line: He showed them his hands, and they were overjoyed. Then he said it again, “Peace be with you,” and gave the frightened friends a job.

steps.q: He also tells them: if you forgive anyone’s sins, they are forgiven. Catholics see the start of which sacrament here?
steps.why: John 20:23. The Council of Trent pointed to this verse for the sacrament of penance: friends who had just been forgiven are sent out to forgive.

steps.line: Then he breathed on them and said, “Receive the Holy Spirit.” The locked room was not the end of the story.
He had once taught: if you bring a gift to the altar and remember someone has something against you, leave it there. First make peace, then come back.
steps.label: a saying of Jesus

steps.line: Today, just before communion at Mass, everyone turns to whoever is beside them, even a stranger, and says, “Peace be with you.”
steps.label: today

steps.q: Today the sign of peace is often a handshake. What did early Christians share instead?
steps.why: Paul tells the churches to “greet one another with a holy kiss.” The kiss of peace stayed in worship for centuries; now it’s often a handshake, a bow or a nod.

say: here’s what i love. the friends who ran away get peace, not a lecture. that’s the first word of easter night.

catholics carry it into every mass. before the table, you turn to whoever is there, not just your best friend. the gesture changes from place to place, a handshake, a bow, a nod. the meaning stays: peace first, then the table.

steps.q: The friends were the ones who ran. So who made the first move toward peace?
o: The friends, by unlocking the door
Peter, speaking for all of them
Jesus, the one who’d been let down
steps.why: The one who was wronged went first. The sign of peace hands that pattern to every Mass, just before people walk up to the altar.

today.say: think of one person you’re not at peace with. you don’t have to fix it today. just wish them peace: in a prayer, if you pray, or in a quiet moment if you don’t.
options: then you’ve already turned toward them. that’s the sign.
that counts. peace usually starts as a thought.
